Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, match, one word or complete the table).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) Seeds used by a farmer are ______ goods. (b) Tractors used by a farmer are ______ goods.
State True or False: (a) Transfer of services is not possible. (b) Consumer goods help in producing other goods.
questions.answer:
(a) True.
(b) False — producer goods help in producing other goods; consumer goods satisfy wants directly.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What is the importance of creating infrastructure?
questions.answer: Infrastructure means energy, transport, communication, health, education and housing. It is the base on which all production rests. Without it the all-round development of the country is not possible.

questions.q: 20 kg of potatoes are sold for a TR of ₹220. Find AR.
questions.answer: AR = TR ÷ Q = 220 ÷ 20 = ₹11 per kg (equal to the price).

questions.q: Distinguish between demand and desire.
questions.answer:
Desire is a mere wish to have a good.
Demand is desire backed by the ability (money) and willingness to pay the price. A wish for a car without the money to buy it is only a desire.

or.answer: Demand changes with the season: ice, coolers and cold drinks in summer, umbrellas and raincoats in the rainy season, woollens in winter.

questions.q: Draw a supply curve and give the reason for its shape.
questions.answer: Plot price on the Y-axis and quantity on the X-axis using a schedule such as ₹1 – 50, ₹2 – 100, ₹3 – 150, ₹4 – 200 units. The curve slopes upward from left to right because price and quantity supplied are directly related: a higher price brings higher profit.

questions.q: Explain the store of value function of money with an example.
questions.answer: Money keeps purchasing power for later use. Sushila cannot store mangoes for long, but she can keep the ₹250 she got by selling them and spend it later.

questions.q: How many types of banks are there in India? Name them.
questions.answer: Four: (1) the Reserve Bank of India, the central bank; (2) commercial banks; (3) cooperative banks; (4) development banks.

questions.q: Draw a simple bar diagram for: Rajasthan 200, Punjab 400, Gujarat 150, Kerala 300 management colleges.
questions.answer:
Take the states on the X-axis and the number of colleges on the Y-axis (scale: 1 cm = 100).
Draw four vertical bars of equal width with equal gaps, of heights 2 cm, 4 cm, 1.5 cm and 3 cm.
Give a title and label both axes.

questions.q: Write the short-cut (assumed mean) formula for the arithmetic mean.
questions.answer: X̄ = A + Σfd ÷ N, where A is the assumed mean, d = x − A, f is the frequency and N = Σf. For an individual series, X̄ = A + Σd ÷ N.

questions.q: What is the share of the primary sector in national income?
questions.answer: Agriculture contributed more than 50% of national income at independence. Its share fell to about 15% in 2009–10 as industry and services grew.

or.answer: Activities in urban areas other than farming: manufacturing, construction, and gas, water and electricity supply (secondary), and trade, transport, banking and other services (tertiary).

questions.q: Name India's main imports.
questions.answer: Petroleum and lubricants (from OPEC countries such as Iran, the UAE and Saudi Arabia), non-ferrous metals, capital goods such as machinery and transport equipment, and fertilisers.

questions.q: What is water pollution? Name two sources.
questions.answer:
Water pollution is the contamination of rivers, lakes, seas and groundwater by untreated wastes.
Sources: sewage from towns, industrial effluents, farm runoff of pesticides and fertilisers, oil spills.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain the four factor incomes.
questions.answer:
(1) Rent: paid to the landlord for the services of land.
(2) Wages: paid to labourers for their physical or mental work.
(3) Interest: paid to the owners of capital, e.g. a bank that lends money to buy a tractor.
(4) Profit: earned by the entrepreneur for organising production and bearing risk.

questions.q: What are the factors affecting individual demand?
questions.answer:
(1) Price of the commodity.
(2) Prices of related goods — substitutes and complements.
(3) Income of the buyer — normal and inferior goods.
(4) Tastes, preferences and fashion.

questions.q: 'The lack of double coincidence of wants is a common problem with the barter system.' Explain.
questions.answer:
In barter, the person with rice who wants cloth must find someone who has cloth and wants rice.
Such a match is rare, so exchange often does not take place and much time is wasted searching, especially when transport and communication were poor.
Money solves this, since anyone accepts money for their goods.

questions.q: Describe the steps in opening a savings account in a bank.
questions.answer:
(1) Visit the bank and ask for an account-opening form.
(2) Fill in the form with name, address and nominee details and attach photographs and proof of identity and address (KYC).
(3) Deposit the minimum initial amount.
(4) The bank opens the account, gives an account number and issues a passbook and cheque book for deposits and withdrawals.

questions.q: Calculate the mean: marks 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 with f = 3, 7, 8, 5, 3, 4.
What is noise pollution? What are its effects?
questions.answer:
Noise pollution is excessive, displeasing noise from traffic, industry, construction and appliances.
Effects: annoyance and aggression, stress, hypertension, sleep disturbance, heart problems and noise-induced hearing loss.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the production activities of the secondary sector and its role in the economy.
questions.answer:
Activities: (1) manufacturing — small-scale (shoes, textiles, furniture) and large-scale (steel, automobiles); (2) construction — buildings, roads, bridges, dams; (3) gas, water and electricity supply.
Role: (1) its share of national income rose from 14% at independence to 28% in 2009–10; (2) it employs about 3.3 crore people; (3) it builds infrastructure — roads, railways, dams such as Hirakud and Bhakra-Nangal, towers; (4) it supplies consumer goods such as clothes, soap, cycles and cars.

questions.q: What kinds of knowledge are needed for consumer awareness?
questions.answer:
(1) Knowledge of the product's quality — whether it is good for health and safe for the environment.
(2) Education about the hazards of marketing — misleading advertisements must be verified.
(3) Knowledge of consumer rights — to get the right product and to claim compensation under the law if it is faulty.
(4) Knowledge of the consumer's own responsibilities — no wasteful or unnecessary consumption, demanding a bill, being a green consumer.
